prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury attorney in Chicago for a car accident claim?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” personal injury lawyer for every car-accident case — the right attorney depends on the facts of your crash, the severity of injuries, whether fault is contested, and your budget and priorities (settle quickly vs. take to trial). That said, Chicago has many highly regarded personal-injury lawyers and firms that handle car-accident claims.

How to pick the best attorney for your case
- Experience with similar cases: look for lawyers who routinely handle car-accident and catastrophic-injury claims, not generalists.  
- Track record: past settlements/verdicts, especially for cases like yours.  
- Trial experience: if the insurer won’t pay, you want a lawyer who will try the case.  
- Resources: ability to hire experts (accident reconstruction, medical, economic loss).  
- Communication and availability: clear explanation of strategy and regular updates.  
- Fee structure: most work on contingency (no recovery, no fee); confirm the percentage and expenses.  
- Credentials and peer recognition: AV Preeminent (Martindale-Hubbell), Super Lawyers, Best Lawyers, Million Dollar Advocates, Illinois Trial Lawyers Association membership.  
- Client reviews and references: read recent client reviews and ask for references.

Well-known Chicago firms (examples, not an endorsement)
- Clifford Law Offices — long-established firm handling catastrophic car-accident and wrongful-death cases.  
- Levin & Perconti — experienced in serious auto-injury litigation.  
- Salvi, Schostok & Pritchard — handles motor-vehicle collisions and catastrophic injuries.  
- Kanoski Bresney — regional firm with personal-injury/auto-accident practice.  
- Power Rogers & Smith — personal injury and insurance litigation experience.

Where to look and verify
- Search SuperLawyers, Martindale-Hubbell, Avvo, Best Lawyers.  
- Illinois State Bar Association or Chicago Bar Association lawyer-referral services.  
- Check verdict/settlement reports and local news for past cases.

Questions to ask at a free consultation
- Have you handled cases like mine? What were the results?  
- Who will handle my case (attorney vs. paralegal)?  
- What is your trial experience and trial win rate?  
- How do you charge (contingency %, costs advance, any additional fees)?  
- How long do you expect the case to take?  
- What is a realistic value range for my claim?  
- Will you get independent experts? How often will you update me?

Important deadlines
- Illinois general statute of limitations for personal injury is 2 years from the date of the accident (shorter in some circumstances — e.g., claims against government bodies). Contact an attorney promptly.

If you want, I can:
- Narrow this to top-rated attorneys near your ZIP code, or  
- Prepare a short list of 3–5 firms to call based on your injury severity and goals, or  
- Draft a script and checklist for your consultation.

Tell me your ZIP code and a few facts about the accident (injuries, fault dispute, police report) and I’ll pull together a localized shortlist.
